response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, cu.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM Customers cu LEFT JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id WHERE cu.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.gender), s AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, 1.0 * order_count / NULLIF(SUM(order_count) OVER (PARTITION BY gender), 0) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT customer_id, gender, order_count, share, share - avg_share AS gap_above_average FROM a WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY (share - avg_share) IS NULL, (share - avg_share) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Customers with no orders are kept with an order count of 0 (and so a share of 0) and count toward the average share across customers.
'No gender recorded' means gender IS NULL. Empty strings are treated as recorded values.

Share is a customer's order count divided by the total orders of all customers with the same gender. The average share is the simple average of those shares over all listed customers, and the gap is share minus that average.

alternatives.interpretation: Only customers who have placed at least one order are considered, so zero-order customers are excluded from the average share.
